title: INSTA: An Ultra-Fast, Differentiable, Statistical Static Timing Analysis Engine for Industrial Physical Design Applications
problem: GPU-accelerated STA (static timing analysis) fails to gain adoption because it cannot emulate proprietary delay models of commercial tools; high-accuracy incremental timing for iterative design loops is slow.
method: GPU-STA initialized from reference commercial tool (one-time setup), then fine-tuned to model tool's delay characteristics. Differentiable engine enables gradient computation for timing optimization; demonstrated on gate sizing and placement tasks with 25x faster incremental updates.

title: Reinforcement Learning-Driven Window Selection for Enhanced Window-Based Rip-up and Reroute in Chip Detailed Routing
problem: Window-based rip-up and reroute in detailed routing is the most runtime-intensive step due to inefficient window selection that targets violations uniformly, wasting effort on low-congestion areas while missing high-congestion routing hotspots.
method: A reinforcement learning approach dynamically generates windows by adjusting size and position based on design rule violation (DRV) distribution, targeting high-congestion areas efficiently. RL learns predictive window placement that minimizes DRVs, achieving high-quality routing results with competitive runtime.

title: RL4Sys: A Lightweight System-driven RL Framework for Drop-in Integration in System Optimization
problem: Reinforcement learning shows promise for system optimization but existing frameworks (RLlib, Ray) introduce substantial integration overhead when embedded in system software, limiting practical deployment.
method: RL4Sys: lightweight RL framework designed for seamless system-level integration. Minimal client embeds in target system to record trajectories and run cached policy inference. Remote trainers execute asynchronously via zero-copy gRPC with adaptive batching.

title: T2-RELION: Task Parallelism, Tensor Core Accelerated RELION for Cryo-EM 3D Reconstruction
problem: RELION's computational efficiency during cryo-EM 3D reconstruction remains a bottleneck due to inefficient parallelization strategies and suboptimal GPU memory management.
method: Optimized RELION implementation introducing: task-level parallelism, three-phase GPU memory management strategy, and Tensor Core acceleration for difference calculation kernels with advanced pipelining for latency hiding and data reuse.

title: MetaSapiens: Real-Time Neural Rendering with Efficiency-Aware Pruning and Accelerated Foveated Rendering
problem: Point-Based Neural Rendering (PBNR), particularly 3D Gaussian Splatting, is computationally too expensive to run in real time on mobile devices due to the large number of Gaussian primitives and the full-resolution rendering required.
method: MetaSapiens combines two techniques: (1) efficiency-aware pruning that reduces the number of Gaussian primitives based on their contribution to rendering quality, using a pruning criterion that accounts for both visual importance and computational cost on the target hardware; and (2) accelerated foveated rendering that exploits the human visual system's reduced acuity in peripheral regions by rendering the foveal region at full quality and peripheral regions at lower resolution or with fewer Gaussians, reducing total computation. Both techniques are co-designed with the mobile hardware execution model to maximize throughput.

title: Profile-Guided Temporal Prefetching
problem: Temporal prefetching for irregular memory access patterns (data-dependent structures, pointer-chasing) requires metadata to record and replay past access sequences; existing on-chip metadata storage schemes for temporal prefetchers have limited capacity, and prior software-guided approaches have failed to optimize metadata storage management effectively, leaving temporal prefetching 0.1% over baseline with profile-guided methods.
method: Prophet is a hardware-software co-designed framework that uses profile-guided methods to optimize on-chip metadata storage management for temporal prefetchers. Instead of tracing full access sequences, Prophet profiles programs using lightweight hardware counters, then injects hints (compiler annotations) into the program binary to guide the hardware temporal prefetcher's metadata storage management at runtime. Dynamic tuning of these hints allows the optimized binary to adapt to different program inputs without re-profiling. Prophet is designed to coexist with existing hardware temporal prefetchers: it provides optimized metadata management for frequently executed hot paths while the original hardware-only scheme handles less frequent paths.

title: 5.6 A Power-Efficient CORDIC-Less Digital Polar Transmitter Using 1b DSM-Based PA Supporting 256-QAM
problem: Digital polar transmitters require CORDIC for I/Q-to-polar conversion but CORDIC's nonlinearity causes bandwidth expansion of AM/PM outputs, challenging wideband implementations. Switched-capacitor PAs suffer low efficiency at power backoff; existing AM/PM modulation methods (PI, DTC, VMD SCPA) introduce further nonlinearity requiring complex DPD.
method: CORDIC-less digital polar transmitter using intrinsically linear 1-bit PA directly supporting polar AM/PM. Edge-selection-based phase modulation replaces CORDIC. 1-bit DSM-based PA inherently avoids switch-capacitor losses and maintains linearity without digital pre-distortion.

title: FineRR-ZNS: Enabling Fine-Granularity Read Refreshing for ZNS SSDs
problem: Zoned namespace SSDs lack read refreshing mechanisms to guarantee data reliability, and zone-level read refreshing incurs severe overhead due to large valid data movements, degrading I/O performance.
method: Proposes host-controlled fine-granularity read refreshing via metadata remapping at block level, includes zone reconstruction method to retrieve remapped data forming complete data, keeps remapped data available and prioritized for read access until next refresh cycle.

title: IRGNN: A Graph-based Framework Integrating Numerical Solution and Point Cloud for Static IR Drop Prediction
problem: IR drop analysis in on-chip power grids is computationally expensive; traditional numerical methods are accurate but slow, while CNN-based ML methods lose fine-grained topology and PG structure information.
method: IRGNN combines numerical solver (AMG-PCG) to generate rough solutions as ground truth with graph-based learning: treats PG nodes as point clouds, extracts features via graph transformer and novel Neighbor Distance Attention (NDA) layer for distance-aware aggregation, capturing both local and global PG topology.

title: X-SAT: An Efficient Circuit-Based SAT Solver
problem: Verifying equivalence of arithmetic circuits requires efficient SAT solving, but existing SAT solvers optimized for CNF struggle with circuit-specific structure and the high variable/clause counts in complex arithmetic circuits.
method: X-SAT integrates Conflict-Driven Clause Learning (CDCL) with structural elimination techniques that reduce variables and clauses while preserving circuit topology. It enhances branching heuristics specifically for arithmetic circuit structure to guide search more efficiently.

title: Helix: Serving Large Language Models over Heterogeneous GPUs and Network via Max-Flow
problem: Serving LLMs across heterogeneous GPU clusters (differing GPU types, memory capacities, and interconnect speeds) is inefficient because existing systems cannot jointly optimize model placement and request scheduling to account for both GPU and network heterogeneity simultaneously.
method: Helix models the LLM inference computation over a heterogeneous cluster as a max-flow problem on a directed, weighted graph where nodes represent GPU instances and edge capacities encode both GPU compute throughput and network bandwidth. A Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) solver operates on this graph to jointly discover optimized model placement (which layers/shards go where) and request scheduling (how tokens are routed through the cluster), treating the two tasks as a unified optimization rather than solving them independently.

title: LLMs Meet Post-Silicon Test Engineering: A New Era (Invited)
problem: Post-silicon test engineering requires domain-specific expertise; AI automation of test tasks is limited by lack of domain grounding.
method: Two-stage LLM-based AI agent framework for post-silicon test engineering: (1) reasoning stage interprets user queries using LLM capabilities, (2) grounding stage executes tasks by integrating LLM outputs with existing test infrastructure. Case study: Intelligent Engineering Assistant (IEA) demonstrates autonomous task execution within established test framework.

title: TCAD Based Study of String Current Variability in 3D NAND Flash Memory
problem: Process variations during etching, deposition, and lithography cause significant variability in string current and electrical properties of 3D NAND flash memory cells, impacting device performance and reliability at advanced technology nodes.
method: Technology Computer-Aided Design (TCAD) simulations to investigate the impact of dimensional variations (cell spacing, tunneling/blocking oxide thickness, channel thickness, plug depth) on string current and critical electrical parameters.

title: When Mitigations Backfire: Timing Channel Attacks and Defense for PRAC-Based RowHammer Mitigations
problem: The JEDEC DDR5 Per Row Activation Counting (PRAC) mechanism and its Alert Back-Off (ABO) protocol and Refresh Management (RFM) commands introduce observable timing differences that create a new timing side-channel, allowing attackers to monitor memory access latencies and infer sensitive information such as cryptographic keys.
method: The paper first presents PRACLeak, a timing channel attack that exploits latency variations induced by ABO protocol and RFM commands to extract secret keys from vulnerable AES implementations by monitoring memory access timing. To counter this, the authors propose Timing-Safe PRAC (TPRAC), which replaces activity-triggered RFM commands with Timing-Based RFMs issued periodically and independently of memory activity, eliminating the observable correlation between memory access patterns and mitigation timing. TPRAC requires only a single-entry in-DRAM mitigation queue per bank and is designed to be compatible with existing DRAM standards.

title: MiniWear: Minimizing Flash Wear via Hybrid Persistent Cache for Extended EF-SMR Lifetime
problem: EF-SMR (Embedded-Flash SMR) systems combine NAND flash and Shingled Magnetic Recording disks to balance cost/performance, but flash endurance faces critical degradation due to high traffic-to-capacity ratios causing excessive wear.
method: MiniWear introduces a hybrid persistent cache (PC) composed of Flash-PC and SMR-PC tiers with fine-grained scheduling strategies. At hardware level, the PC is organized as dual tiers; at software level, customized scheduling manages PC resources efficiently. Proactive balancing strategy addresses resource idleness to maximize wear distribution across storage layers.

title: Molten Chloride Small Modular Reactor Performance Characteristics for Data Center Operation
problem: Data centers require high-reliability power; conventional large nuclear reactors have large footprint. Molten chloride small modular reactors (SMRs) promising but behavior under data center load profiles (mismatched power rating, sub-maximum capacity) unexplored.
method: MOOSE (Multiphysics Object Oriented Simulation Environment) framework simulation of molten salt SMR. Control rods at 60% open (below-maximum capacity operation). Analysis of steady-state thermal-hydraulic behavior.
